content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: HIGH urgency — inference-queue backlog exceeded threshold for 5m. Service: inference-router. Pager: oncall@redwood.com

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident triggered: INC5990012345 — inference-queue backlog surge (auto-escalation enabled).

ben (oncall): ack. I'm taking primary. Currently getting a lot of 429s from edge and elevated queue depth. @channel pls chime in if you're already looking. :eyes:

alice (sre): seeing the same. Metrics: queue_depth ~ 48k, processing rate dropped ~40%. Autoscaler event stream shows scale attempts but pods are stuck in Pending.

chandra (eng-runtime): confirmed. Runtime logs show repeated gpuscheduler timeouts and repeated "failed to attach volume" for new worker pods. kubectl describe on a stuck pod:```Events:
  Normal  Scheduled  2m    default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/inference-worker-xyz
  Warning FailedAttachVolume  1m  attachdetach-controller  AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "nvme-cache" : rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
```

frank (infra): quick check — cloud quotas are fine but CSI driver is erroring intermittently against the node group. I see a cluster node provisioning spike and some nodes entering NotReady with kubelet OOMKills. Might be instance type hitting driver bug.

ben (oncall): action list: 1) pause noncritical ingestion flows; 2) attempt manual scale (force new node pool) 3) open PD to infra for quota/driver. I'll coordinate.

dan (prod-support): notifying a handful of affected customers who hit elevated latency. Preparing a heads-up template.

maria (eng-platform): can we temporarily lower batch sizes / increase token-timeout to speed throughput while we spin new capacity? That could reduce per-request compute.

ben (oncall): executing:
```bash
# reduce batch size via runtime config
redwoodctl config set runtime.batch.max_size 8 --env prod
# bump nodegroup desired manually
gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize inference-pool --size=24
```

chandra (eng-runtime): applied batch-size bump to 8 and lowered request wait window to 30ms. Visible effect: single-worker latency up slightly but throughput recovered ~15% within 90s.

frank (infra): kicked off manual node group resize and started a new node pool with different instance family to avoid the CSI problem. New nodes are provisioning — cloud shows 8 new instances.

incident-bot: :information_source: Note: autoscaler events halted at 2025-03-18T02:14:10Z due to repeated failures, manual override in progress.

alice (sre): I'm tailing controller-manager logs. HPA saw CPU saturation but scale up failed because pod creation timed out repeatedly. Also hitting EBS attach throttling in us-west1 region.

maria (eng-platform): workaround: routing low-priority inference to a fallback model cluster (lower-spec) to clear the main queue. Deploying a traffic-split rule now.

ben (oncall): traffic-split applied. Less critical traffic rerouted to fallback cluster. Primary queue depth dropping from 48k -> 19k in last 6m. :thumbsup:

eva (customer-success): looping in CS; sending proactive notice to impacted customers with ETA update. Template: "We're addressing an internal capacity issue affecting inference response times; mitigation is underway."

chandra (eng-runtime): new nodes Ready. Kubelet attaching volumes successfully now. Pods entering Running and warming KV caches. Queue processing rate back to ~85% of normal.

frank (infra): driver's upstream reported a transient regression; we've pinned node image to previous stable and opened a bug. Node pool with pinned image is healthy.

ben (oncall): summary so far: autoscaler attempted to scale but pod attach failures prevented effective scaling; manual node pool + batch-size changes + traffic split regained capacity. Continuing to monitor for 30m.

alice (sre): capturing next steps: 1) Postmortem owner? 2) add tighter alerts for attach-failure rate; 3) test autoscaler with simulated attach failures. I'll take postmortem.

maria (eng-platform): I'll add a fallback routing policy to be auto-enabled on attach-failure spikes. Also will add a limiter to prevent heavy non-prod jobs from consuming infer pool during surge.

dan (prod-support): CS update sent. Keeping customers informed.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC5990012345 acknowledged by ben (oncall). Escalation paused.

ben (oncall): marking incident as under control. Will keep this thread for coordination — aim to resolve and close in 2 hours after validation. If anything regresses, re-fire PD.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident stabilized. Please add notes for follow-up and link any logs.

alice (sre): postmortem assigned to alice. Timeline dump: attach failures started 02:11Z, PD fired 02:14Z, manual nodepool provisioned 02:21Z, traffic-split 02:24Z, new nodes Ready 02:30Z, queue steady 02:40Z.

frank (infra): opened infra ticket INF-2043 with vendor logs and pinned image change noted.

maria (eng-platform): created follow-up tasks: FPL-88 (auto-fallback on attach failure), FPL-89 (autoscaler resiliency test harness).

eva (customer-success): continuing customer outreach for next 2 hours while we validate.

ben (oncall): thanks everyone. Leaving a final note here when fully closed. For now, lowering alert noise. :handshake:
